title: Distributed open justice oversight (DOJO): A community-driven, modality-agnostic platform for adversarial evaluation of health AI
venue: SSRN preprint 6676818, not peer reviewed (version dated 2026-04-29)

cost.compute_notes: PDF supplied at dojo/literature/xiang2026dojo.pdf (210,641 bytes, 11 pp), read in full. Checked the advertised install and the public repo with gh/curl; nothing to run.

triggers: what is DOJO distributed open justice oversight
platform for adversarial evaluation of clinical AI
data plane model plane clinical workflow plane
community participatory evaluation of health AI
shortcut detection agent for medical imaging

claims.statement: DOJO is proposed as an open-source, containerised, MCP-based evaluation layer between data access and clinical deployment, with three planes (data: shortcuts, cohort bias, measurement equity; model: adversarial and out-of-distribution inputs; clinical workflow: latency, GPU, interoperability), a human-in-the-loop layer, and installation via `pip install dojo-health`.
claims.scope: A position/design paper. Version 1.0 'is planned to ship' three MCP agents across two planes; Aim 3's comparative study (5-10 models, blinded expert panels, pre-registered) is future work.

our_assessment.why: As a statement of intent, accurate. As of 2026-09-30 no platform is released: `dojo-health` returns 404 on PyPI (an invented-name control also 404s; bodhi-llm returns 200, so the check discriminates), and criticaldata/dojo is a static website. The empirical arms that exist are separate papers (cajas2026-agents-catching-agents, cajas2026-modalens).

claims.statement: Evaluators are recalibrated by interleaving adversarial decoy results from randomised data at 5-10% of evaluations; misclassifying a decoy triggers disclosure and retraining, repeated failures down-weight the evaluator, and each evaluator's calibration score accompanies any certification they sign.

our_assessment.why: The idea is sound and old in other fields: it is the catch-trial / attention-check logic of psychophysics and crowdsourcing, and the 'known-answer' test this KB applies to its own instruments. The paper names the second-order risk (evaluators learning to spot decoys) and proposes refreshing decoys; whether a 5-10% rate gives a usable per-evaluator calibration score depends on how many evaluations one evaluator does (at 50 evaluations, 2.5-5 decoys), which the paper does not address.

claims.statement: The BODHI framework, 'validated across 1,800 observations with very large effect sizes (Cohen's d = 16.38-19.54)', provides the measurement methodology for evaluator epistemic virtues.

our_assessment.why: The cited BMJ paper reports 2,000 observations (200 vignettes x 5 seeds x 2 models), not 1,800, and its d values are standardised by seed-to-seed spread of 200-case means (arslan2026-bodhi-engineering#c2). Standardised per response, the same rates give d = 4.0 and 2.4. The acronym is also expanded differently: 'Bridging, Open, Discerning, Humble, Inquiring' here and in the library README, 'Balanced, Open-minded, Diagnostic, Humble, Inquisitive' in the BMJ paper.

claims.statement: Background figures quoted as motivation: LMM performance on rare anatomical variants falls from about 74% to 29%; 'mirage' fabrication without image input exceeds 60% and reaches 90-100% under common prompting; only 3.6% of FDA-cleared AI/ML devices reported race/ethnicity, 81.6% omitted age, 9.0% had a post-market surveillance plan; MIMIC yields about 452 citations per million dollars against 14 (UK Biobank) and 0.4 (All of Us).

our_assessment.why: Recorded so they are findable, marked unverified so nobody quotes them from here. The citations-per-dollar ratio comes from a medRxiv preprint by overlapping authors (ref 28).

checked.result: Read. Note first-listed author is Tohyama; the file name and the citation used by the group (e.g. ref 21 of arXiv:2608.03744) put Xiang first. Record id follows the group's citation key.

checked.how: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://pypi.org/pypi/dojo-health/json (404); controls: .../bodhi-llm/json (200), .../zz-invented-pkg-qq/json (404); gh api repos/criticaldata/dojo/contents
checked.result: No PyPI package. The GitHub repo is a static website (index.html, styles.css; default branch feat/dojo-website-native, pushed 2026-09-30) that explicitly contains no evaluation services. The paper says 'planned', so this is not a broken promise, just nothing to run yet.

relations.why: Aim 2 rests on BODHI's measurement methodology.
relations.asymmetric_note: Cites 1,800 observations where the source says 2,000.

open_questions: How many decoys does one evaluator see before their calibration score has a usable interval? At a 5-10% decoy rate that is a question about evaluator workload, and it decides whether the score is signal.
The zoo's own dojo/ workspace borrows the name for a contribution workflow; it is not the DOJO platform. Keep the two distinct in any writing.
